11.title: Carlos asks about a house on Zillow
11.gist: A new buyer asks if a house is available, if he can see it Saturday, and if the area is safe with good schools. The assistant writes Sam a reply to approve.
did: Saved Carlos as a new lead.
Wrote a friendly reply email and a short phone script for Sam.
Did not write a text message, because Carlos never said texting was OK.
After Sam sent the email, it noted the date and set a reminder to follow up.
rules: Didn't give an opinion on safety or schools. That's a fair housing rule. It pointed Carlos to the police crime map and state school report cards instead.
Put the Texas brokerage notice (IABS) link right in the email, as Texas requires when you first discuss a specific home.
Told Carlos a written buyer agreement is needed before any showing (Texas law since 2026).
Didn't say the house was still available until Sam checked.

12.title: Sam calls Carlos and sizes him up
12.gist: Before the call, the assistant gives Sam a short list of questions. After the call, it scores how ready Carlos is to buy.
did: Made a one-page call script that only asks what Sam doesn't already know.
Read Sam's call notes: new job in January, pre-approved for $510k, wants to close by mid-December.
Scored Carlos 9 out of 11: a "hot" lead. Next step: book a meeting right away.
rules: Asked first whether Carlos already had an agent. You can't take another agent's client.
Only scored what Carlos actually said. Things not discussed were left as questions for next time.
Marked texting as OK only after Carlos said yes on the call.

13.title: Sam meets Carlos in person
13.gist: The assistant prepares a meeting packet. After the meeting, it saves what Carlos wants in a home.
did: Wrote a meeting packet: how buying works, the buyer agreement, loan options, and a wish-list worksheet.
After the meeting, saved Carlos's search: up to $500k, 3+ bedrooms, a garage, three Round Rock zip codes.
Recorded that Carlos signed the buyer agreement, which means tours can now happen.
rules: Explained the two Texas buyer agreement options: full representation, or a 14-day "just showing" agreement.
Didn't write any contract wording. Sam uses the brokerage's official forms.
Listed two lenders and said Carlos doesn't have to use either.

14.title: Finding homes that fit
14.gist: The assistant checks five listings against Carlos's wish list and picks the best three.
did: Dropped two homes: one had only a carport, one was outside his areas.
Ranked the other three and flagged any priced close to his loan limit.
Noted that one of the homes is listed by Sam's own brokerage.
rules: Searched only by what Carlos asked for (price, size, garage, area). Never by who lives in a neighborhood.
Flagged the home listed by Sam's own brokerage. In Texas, both sides must agree in writing before Sam can advise on it.
Wrote "unknown, check listing" instead of guessing missing facts like HOA fees.

15.title: Saturday tours
15.gist: The assistant plans a driving route for three showings, then records what Carlos thought of each house.
did: Planned the tour in driving order, about 45 minutes per house.
Logged Carlos's reactions. Oak Bend got a 5 out of 5 and he'd make an offer. Pecan Hollow is the backup.
Offered to check Oak Bend's value now; Sam chose to wait until the offer.
rules: Checked the buyer agreement was signed before planning any tour.
Didn't contact any listing agents itself. Sam asks for the showings.
Tour notes describe the houses ("busy road", "dated"), never the neighbors.

16.title: Making an offer on Oak Bend
16.gist: The assistant checks what the house is worth and suggests an offer. The seller counters, and they agree on $482,000.
did: Compared recent nearby sales. The house is worth about $478k–$492k, most likely $485k.
Suggested opening at $480,000 with normal protections.
The seller countered at $485k. Carlos countered at $482k and the seller said yes.
rules: Didn't suggest paying extra if the appraisal comes in low, because Carlos wouldn't have enough cash left.
Produced a summary of terms only. Sam fills in the official Texas contract form.
No "love letter" to the seller, since those can cause fair housing problems.
Spotted that Carlos's budget for this house ($490k) differed from his saved search ($500k), and asked instead of guessing.

17.title: Under contract: the clock starts
17.gist: The contract is signed. The assistant turns it into a calendar of every deadline so nothing gets missed.
did: Read back every date and dollar amount for Sam to confirm.
Built the deadline calendar: deposits due 11/5, the option period (Carlos's window to back out) ends 11/9 at 5 p.m., closing 12/4.
Drafted a kick-off email to Carlos and emails to the title company and lender.
rules: Used only numbers from the signed contract and guessed nothing.
Treated the 5 p.m. option deadline as fixed. Missing it costs Carlos his easy way out.
Two seller deadlines fall on a Saturday, so it showed both possible dates and asked Sam's broker.
Warned Carlos about wire fraud: always call the title company to confirm wiring instructions.

18.title: The inspection finds problems
18.gist: With only two business days left in the option period, the assistant turns the inspection report into a short, focused repair request.
did: Confirmed the deposits arrived on time, so Carlos's right to back out still holds.
Sorted 10 findings: 3 safety fixes, 2 big-ticket items (AC and roof, $7,950 credit), 2 other defects, 3 cosmetic items skipped.
Set a plan: send today, seller answers by Friday noon, decide by Monday noon if needed.
rules: Timed everything so the signed agreement lands a day before the deadline.
Only used dollar amounts from real estimates. The rest say "estimate needed".
Left out cosmetic items like paint, because they weaken a repair request.
Quoted the inspector's words instead of interpreting them.

21.title: Dan might sell "next year"
21.gist: A homeowner fills out a website form saying he might sell sometime next year. The assistant writes a reply.
did: Saved Dan as a new seller lead.
Wrote a reply email offering to talk about his home's value.
No text or call script, since Dan didn't give a phone number.
rules: Included the Texas brokerage notice (IABS) link in the email.
Didn't guess a price for his home before doing a proper analysis.
Put the broker's name and license number in the signature, as Texas advertising rules require.

22.title: Not ready yet: staying in touch
22.gist: Dan says spring or summer. The assistant marks him as a "cold" lead and plans a few months of helpful emails.
did: Scored Dan 4 out of 11, which counts as cold.
Wrote seven monthly emails with useful info, not just "checking in".
A few emails ask politely for his phone number.
rules: Email only, since Dan hasn't agreed to calls or texts.
Every email has an unsubscribe line and the brokerage address, as email law requires.
Sam corrected the score: Dan's reason (moving near family) counts and is fine to record.

23.title: Dan suddenly wants to list now
23.gist: Dan bought a home in Dallas and wants to sell fast. The assistant re-scores him and prepares for the listing meeting.
did: Moved Dan from cold to hot and stopped the email plan.
Compared recent nearby sales and recommended listing at $449,000.
Wrote an outline for Sam's listing presentation.
rules: Left out a sale that happened after this date, so the analysis only uses what Sam could know then.
Didn't invent price adjustments it had no local numbers for.
Labeled the analysis "not an appraisal" and left the price decision to Dan.

24.title: Getting the listing live
24.gist: Dan signs and picks $449,000. The assistant writes a launch checklist and all the marketing copy.
did: Made a dated checklist: paperwork, photos, the sign, going live on 10/10.
Wrote the MLS description, three social posts, an email and flyer bullets.
Turned down Dan's wording "perfect for a growing family" and "master suite", and gave Sam a simple explanation for Dan.
rules: Fair housing: listings describe the house, not who should live there.
Uses "primary bedroom" instead of "master".
The broker's name goes on every ad, as Texas requires.
Described the kitchen honestly as original.

25.title: How's the listing doing?
25.gist: After four showings and no offers, the assistant writes Dan an honest weekly report.
did: Logged what each buyer's agent said. All four mentioned the dated kitchen.
Flagged three signs that it's time to talk about price or the kitchen.
Gave Dan three options, each backed by a nearby sale, and left the choice to him.
rules: Recorded feedback about the house only, nothing about the buyers.
Presented price signals as a conversation, not a demand.
Refused to peek at offers dated after the report date.

26.title: Three offers at once
26.gist: Three offers arrive. The assistant compares what Dan would actually take home and how likely each is to close. Dan picks the cash offer.
did: Lined up all three offers by when they expire.
Estimated Dan's take-home for each. The highest price ($452k) only nets about $3.6k more, and it's the riskiest.
Dan accepts the $438k cash offer and asks the $445k buyer to be the backup.
rules: Compared take-home money and certainty, not just price.
Never shared one buyer's offer with another. Two agents from the same office got separate emails.
Noticed none of the offers listed an option fee. It has to be filled in before Dan signs.
